full_judgment: Md. Ruhul Amin, J: Petitioner, Chairman, at the relevant time, of Bangladesh Co-operative Insurance Ltd. has obtained this Rule under Article 102 (2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned order No. 449-Pa Dated: -2.6.1991 communicated to him under Memo No. 10/91-449(4) পরিকল্পনা dated: 2.6.1991 (Annexure-G to the petition) passed by the Respondent No. 3 Mr. Mostafizur Rahman, Arbitrator Joint Registrar (planning) Co-operative Societies. Bangladesh in Dispute Case No. 3 of 1991 under Section 86 of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance 1984 (Ordinance No. I of 1985) staying operation of the order of dismissal till disposal to the Dispute case shall not be declared to be illegal and to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why the proceedings of Dispute Case No. 3 shall not be declared to be illegal, void and inoperative or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. Facts, in short, are that Managing Committee of the Bangladesh Cooperative Insurance Ltd. hereinafter in brief Insurance Company, constituted an enquiry committee to enquire into the activities of the Insurance Company and the enquiry committee after preliminary enquiry submitted its report to the Chairman of the Insurance Company regarding the conduct, performance, activities of the then General Manager and Chief Executive Syed Md. Habibul Huq (Respondent No. 4); that the Insurance Company on receipt of the report served show-cause notice dated 17.3.1991 to the Respondent No. 4 asking him to give his reply as to why he shall not be dismissed from the service and steps, for realization of the money misappropriated shall not be taken; that allegations against the said respondent being of serious nature placed him under suspension, that the enquiry committee submitted final report on 25.3.1991 as regards conduct, performance and the activities of the respondent no. 4; that thereupon formal charges were brought against the said respondent by the Insurance Company's letter dated 4.4.1991; that as against the order of suspension respondent no. 4 filed Dispute Case No. 1 of 1991 (Dugdha) before the Registrar of Cooperative Societies and the Registrar appointed Respondent No. 3 sole Arbitrator in the said Arbitration case, that the Arbitrator by an ad-interim order dated 14.4.1991 stayed operation of the order of suspension, that the Insurance Company made representation to the Arbitrator for withdrawing the exparte order of stay dated 14.4.1991 but without any result, that in due course departmental enquiry was conducted in respect of the allegations and charges brought earlier against the Respondent No. 4; that at the time of conducting the enquiry he was given all the opportunities available in law; that the respondent no. 4 did not submit his reply to the charges inspite of receipt of the same nor appeared before the enquiry officer inspite of being informed duly and that in the said background enquiry was completed ex parte; that on receipt of the report of the enquiry committee the respondent no. 4 was served with the 2nd show cause notice and this time also he did not submit his reply, that in due course the Insurance Company took decision to dismiss him and ultimately dismissed him with effect from 28.5.1991 and informed him of the same by the letter dated 28.5.1991; that as against the order of dismissal the respondent no. 4 filed Dispute Case No. 3 of 1991 (Dudgha) to the Registrar of the Co-operative Societies who thereupon appointed respondent no. 3 as the Arbitrator; that the Arbitrator stayed the operation of the order of dismissal dated 28.5.1991 by the impugned order dated 2.6.1991.
